atoms.text: Now Milo is going to show you around some tropical rainforests.

instruction.text: Select the photo of the tropical rainforest.

hint.label: Tropical
hint.text: Tropical is another way of saying warm and wet. We can also call this climate humid.

feedback.end: Correct! Tropical rainforests are forests found in warm and wet climates near to the Equator. They are home to lots and lots of animals, such as monkeys like Milo!

instruction.text: This is a tropical rainforest in Thailand. Select the tops of the trees to learn more about tropical rainforests.

text: This part of the forest is called the canopy. In tropical rainforests, this is where most of the animals live.

instruction.text: Let’s do some fieldwork! Milo wants to know how much it rains in the rainforest each day.

feedback.correct: Exactly! A rain gauge collects rainwater and has a measurement on the side. Milo can check the rain gauge each day to record how much it has rained.
feedback.wrong: A fork would not be very useful for measuring rain.

atoms.a: Which other tool might be useful for Milo?

feedback.correct: Milo can use the notepad to write down how much it rains each day. Milo will probably record a lot of rain in the rainforest!
feedback.wrong: A hosepipe would not be very useful for measuring rain.

atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m7'>What does a rain gauge do</voice>

b.sound: It collects rainwater, so you can measure how much it has rained.
It sucks all of the water out of the clouds.

atoms.a: “Where do most animals in the rainforest live?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m7'> Where do most animals in the rainforest live</voice>
ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m7'>What are tropical rainforests</voice>

b.sound: They are wet forests in hot climates near to the Equator.
They are very cold forests in the north of the planet.
